Users of ProVerif

If you have written a research paper or a tool using ProVerif, or teach a course on ProVerif, and want it to be added to this page, or if you want the reference to your paper/tool/course to be removed or corrected, please contact Bruno Blanchet.

Research papers

350+ publications have used ProVerif, including 60+ in rank A* or A conferences, according to ICORE conference ranking 2026.

We list publications in rank A* or A conferences below. Click here for the full list.

Tools

  • TulaFale, analyzer for Web services, using ProVerif as a back-end (Microsoft Research).
  • FS2PV, verifier for protocol implementations written in F#, using ProVerif as a back-end (Microsoft Research).
  • Spi2Java (manual available here) also allows using ProVerif as protocol analyzer for their protocol specifications (using the Spi2Proverif auxiliary tool).
  • Expi2Java also allows using ProVerif as protocol analyzer for their protocol specifications (project apparently stopped).
  • A ProVerif editor (in Python) by Joeri de Ruiter.
  • XOR-ProVerif and DH-ProVerif: tools for verifying protocols with XOR and with Diffie-Hellman exponentiation (with a rich equational theory).
  • StatVerif: extension of ProVerif to verify stateful processes.
  • TTool uses ProVerif for proving confidentiality and authenticity properties from an AVATAR model.
  • AIF-Omega: Set-based abstraction method inspired by ProVerif and SPASS, for verifying systems with non-monotonic, stateful behaviour. Uses Spass or ProVerif as back-ends.
  • Set-pi supports an extension of the applied pi calculus with sets; it generates clauses fed into ProVerif.
  • AnBx: compiler from Alice and Bob notation to Java, OFMC, and ProVerif.
  • Ukano: automatic privacy verifier. This tool automatically checks unlinkability and anonymity for a large class of 2-party protocols for an unbounded number of sessions.
  • GSVerif: front-end for dealing with global state and counters.
  • Noise explorer verifies Noise protocols, using ProVerif as back-end.
  • SAPIC+ is a security protocol verification platform, enabling the use of ProVerif, Tamarin and DeepSec as possible backends.
